reason: The text depicts Yahweh as actively engaged and responsive to His people, contradicting the characterization as 'remote' and 'emotionally removed.' Specific evidence: God hears the Israelites' groaning (וַיִּשְׁמַע אֱלֹהִים אֶת־ נַאֲקָתָם); God remembers His covenant (וַיִּזְכֹּר אֱלֹהִים אֶת־ בְּרִית); God sees and knows the people (וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים... וַיֵּדַע); God speaks directly to Moses (וַיְדַבֵּר אֱלֹהִים אֶל־ מֹשֶׁה); and God makes covenantal promises of liberation (וְהוֹצֵאתִי אֶתְכֶם, וְהִצַּלְתִּי אֶתְכֶם). These actions demonstrate intimate relational engagement and responsiveness rather than emotional remoteness. While the text does affirm God's power over nature and human affairs, it emphasizes His covenantal commitment and attentiveness to human suffering.
